checklist.step: Trigger inventory intake at model conception
actions: Before any model touches production data, open a New Model Request in the model governance repository.
Complete the mandatory intake fields: business purpose, target variable, input data sources, decision the model influences, and whether a human reviews the output before it acts on a customer.
Tag the model against the risk taxonomy — HIGH for pricing/underwriting/claims-triage, MEDIUM for retention/marketing propensity, LOW for internal ops analytics.
Route the request to the Model Risk Analyst queue and notify the Chief Data Officer team by email.
checklist.done: the request carries a complete field set, a risk tag and is routed for review before the model reaches production.

checklist.step: Classify the model's risk tier and required governance level
actions: Open the intake request and apply the risk-tiering rubric against the stated decision use (pricing, underwriting, claims, fraud, retention, marketing).
Confirm whether the model output is solely automated with no human review, which triggers the UK GDPR Article 22 assessment.
Record the required governance controls for the assigned tier: bias testing cadence, human-oversight documentation, explainability method.
Return the classification to the Data Scientist and copy the Chief Data Officer on HIGH-tier classifications.
checklist.done: the model carries a risk tier, an Article 22 flag and its required control set before build proceeds.

checklist.step: Register model lineage and data sources
actions: In Databricks Lakehouse open the model's Unity Catalog entry and list every source table and feature-engineering pipeline feeding it.
Confirm each source table has a data-quality owner and a documented refresh schedule.
Paste the lineage diagram (or catalog link) into the model governance repository record.
Flag any source containing protected characteristics (age, health, postcode-derived proxies) for the bias-testing team.
checklist.done: the inventory record links to a verified lineage diagram naming every source and its data-quality owner.

checklist.step: Confirm human decision-authority is documented before go-live
actions: Review the intake record's human-oversight field against the model's actual deployment design.
For any HIGH-tier model, confirm a named role can override or reject the model's output before it reaches the customer.
Reject go-live sign-off where no override path exists and send the request back to the model owner.
Record the confirmed human-oversight design on the inventory record.
checklist.done: every HIGH-tier model shows a named override role before the CDO approves go-live.

checklist.step: Log the model into the central inventory with a unique identifier
actions: Assign a unique Model ID in the model governance repository and set status to 'In Production'.
Attach the lineage diagram, risk classification, human-oversight design and the bias-testing schedule.
Set the next scheduled review date per the risk tier (HIGH = quarterly, MEDIUM = semi-annual, LOW = annual).
Publish the record so it is visible to Compliance, Risk and Internal Audit.
checklist.done: the model has a unique inventory record, status 'In Production' and a scheduled review date.

checklist.step: Reconcile the inventory to production deployment logs
actions: Export the list of models registered as 'live' in the Azure ML / MLflow model registry.
Export the list of 'In Production' models from the model governance repository.
Diff the two lists on model name and version; any registry model absent from the inventory is a shadow model.
Log every mismatch as an open item with the deploying team's name for follow-up.
checklist.done: the registry-to-inventory diff is complete and every mismatch has a named follow-up owner.

checklist.step: Investigate and close out shadow-model findings
actions: Open a GRC exception record for each shadow model found in the reconciliation.
Interview the deploying Data Scientist to establish how the model reached production without intake.
Require immediate retrospective completion of the intake, risk classification and lineage steps.
Set a remediation date and escalate to the Chief Risk Officer if the model is HIGH-tier and has been live over 30 days undocumented.
checklist.done: every shadow model has a closed GRC exception with a completed retrospective inventory entry.

checklist.step: Update the inventory on retraining or material model change
actions: On any retrain, feature-set change or target-variable change, open a Model Change record against the existing Model ID.
Re-run the risk classification if the change affects the decision use or data sources.
Version the model in the inventory (e.g. v1.0 to v1.1) and link the new artefact in Azure ML / MLflow.
Notify the Model Risk Analyst that a re-review of bias testing and explainability documentation is due.
checklist.done: the inventory shows the new version, linked artefact and a triggered re-review.

checklist.step: Track model ownership and business-sponsor changes
actions: Run a quarterly ownership report from the model governance repository listing named owner and business sponsor per model.
Cross-check leavers/movers against the HR system and flag any model with an owner no longer in role.
Reassign ownership within 10 business days and update the inventory record.
Confirm the new owner has read and accepted the model's governance obligations.
checklist.done: no inventory record carries an owner who has left the role for more than 10 business days.

checklist.step: Assess third-party and vendor AI models for inventory inclusion
actions: Cross-reference the vendor/outsourcing register for any supplier providing scoring, pricing or claims-triage services driven by AI.
Request the vendor's model documentation (purpose, training data provenance, bias-testing evidence) via the vendor management process.
Register the vendor model in the inventory with source 'Third Party' and link the outsourcing register entry.
Confirm the vendor contract obliges the supplier to notify material model changes.
checklist.done: every vendor-supplied AI model used in a UK decision process has an inventory record linked to its outsourcing register entry.

checklist.step: Decommission models and archive the inventory record
actions: On retirement, set the model status to 'Decommissioned' with the retirement date and reason.
Confirm the model has been removed from the Azure ML / MLflow serving endpoint and Databricks scheduled jobs.
Archive the lineage, bias-test history and change log under the Model ID for the retention period.
Notify Compliance that the model is no longer in production.
checklist.done: the archived record is complete and the serving endpoint is confirmed removed.

checklist.step: Present the inventory summary to the AI Governance Committee
actions: Compile a quarterly summary: total models, new intakes, retirements, open shadow-model exceptions and overdue reviews.
Present the summary at the AI Governance / Risk Committee meeting with the Chief Risk Officer in attendance.
Record committee questions and any required remediation actions in the minutes.
Distribute the approved summary to Compliance and Internal Audit.
checklist.done: the committee has reviewed and minuted the quarterly inventory summary.

checklist.step: Escalate overdue registrations past the 5-business-day SLA
actions: Pull the SLA breach report from the model governance repository for intakes not completed within 5 business days of production deployment.
Contact the model owner directly and request same-week completion.
Escalate any breach exceeding 15 business days to the Chief Risk Officer as a control failure.
Log the escalation and its resolution date.
checklist.done: no intake breach remains open past 15 business days without a logged escalation.

checklist.step: Reconcile inventory scope against new FCA AI guidance
actions: On publication of any new FCA AI-related discussion paper, policy statement or portfolio letter, review the current inventory scope against it.
Identify any model type newly brought into scope (e.g. generative AI used in customer correspondence) and add it to the intake taxonomy.
Brief the Chief Data Officer and Data Science teams on the scope change.
Update the AI Model Inventory Standard accordingly.
checklist.done: the inventory taxonomy is updated within 30 days of any FCA scope-relevant publication.

checklist.step: Retain inventory evidence for the retention period
actions: Export the full inventory, reconciliation logs and decommission archive quarterly into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year-from-retirement retention label to each model's record set.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by Model ID, owner and risk tier.
Verify the prior quarter's export remains retrievable before closing the current cycle.
checklist.done: the quarter's inventory evidence is filed, labelled for 6-year retention and retrievable by Model ID.

testing.step: Build the population of models believed to be in production
actions: Export every model marked 'In Production' from the model governance repository as of the test date.
Independently export every live model/version from the Azure ML / MLflow registry and every scheduled scoring job in Databricks Lakehouse.
Merge the two extracts and reconcile counts before sampling.
Sign the population as complete, including the reconciliation total.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between the inventory and the live registries and signed as complete.

testing.step: Identify shadow models missed by the quarterly reconciliation
actions: List every registry/scheduled-job model absent from the inventory export.
Confirm each was, or was not, already logged as an open GRC exception.
Treat any unreported shadow model as an automatic test exception.
Record the count and names of unreported shadow models in the workpaper.
testing.done: every registry model not in the inventory is either matched to a logged exception or listed as a new exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of HIGH-tier (pricing/underwriting/claims) models.
Take 15 randomly selected MEDIUM/LOW-tier models (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every HIGH-tier model.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk classification for each sampled model
actions: Read the model's stated business purpose and decision use independently of the recorded tier.
Apply the risk-tiering rubric fresh and reach an independent conclusion.
Compare to the recorded tier; any downgrade or upgrade is an exception.
Capture the rubric worksheet used for the re-classification.
testing.done: each sampled model has an independent re-classification note, with any discrepancy logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify lineage and human-oversight documentation on the sample
actions: Open the Unity Catalog lineage for each sampled model and confirm it matches the diagram attached to the inventory record.
Confirm a named override role exists for every HIGH-tier sampled model.
Contact the named override holder to confirm they are aware of the responsibility.
Flag any lineage or oversight documentation that is stale or unconfirmed.
testing.done: lineage matches the live catalog and every HIGH-tier sampled model has a confirmed named overseer.

testing.step: Test third-party model coverage
actions: Cross-check the vendor/outsourcing register against the inventory's 'Third Party' source entries.
Confirm each in-scope vendor model has current bias-testing evidence on file.
Flag any vendor providing AI-driven scoring with no corresponding inventory entry.
Log missing vendor entries as exceptions with the outsourcing register reference.
testing.done: every in-scope vendor AI service traces to an inventory record with current evidence, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm decommissioned models were actually removed from serving
actions: For a sample of records marked 'Decommissioned', query the Azure ML / MLflow serving endpoint and Databricks job scheduler.
Confirm no active endpoint or job references the retired model version.
Flag any decommissioned model still live as a critical exception.
Capture the endpoint/job query results into the workpaper.
testing.done: no sampled decommissioned model is found still serving in production.

testing.step: Check ownership currency on the sample
actions: Confirm the named owner and business sponsor on each sampled record are current employees in the stated role.
Cross-check against the HRIS leavers report for the test period.
Flag any record whose owner left role more than 10 business days before the test date without reassignment.
Record findings by Model ID.
testing.done: no sampled record shows a stale owner beyond the 10-business-day reassignment window.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the Model ID, what was missed and the governance impact.
Assign a root cause (missed intake, stale lineage, unremoved endpoint, ownership drift) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next quarter's mandatory retest.
Confirm each prior-quarter exception was actually closed before marking it resolved.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest status.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for undocumented HIGH-tier models.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who classified none of the sampled models, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the AI Governance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm which models are due for fairness testing
actions: Query the model governance repository for HIGH-tier models with a fairness-test date over 11 months old, or with no test on record.
Cross-check against models flagged for go-live in the next 60 days.
Compile the due list with Model ID, owner and target deadline.
Send the due list to Data Science Lead and the model owners.
checklist.done: the due list is complete and distributed with named owners and deadlines.

checklist.step: Define the protected-characteristic proxy variables to test
actions: Pull the current Equality Act 2010 protected-characteristic list and the approved proxy-variable mapping (postcode as a proxy for ethnicity, occupation as a proxy for disability, etc.) from the Model Fairness Testing Standard.
Identify which proxies are present, directly or via correlated features, in the model's input dataset.
Document any proxy the model owner disputes and escalate to the Data Science Lead for a ruling.
Record the final proxy list on the model's test plan.
checklist.done: the test plan names every protected-characteristic proxy present in the model's inputs, with disputes resolved.

checklist.step: Assemble the holdout dataset with demographic labels
actions: In Databricks Lakehouse, pull a representative holdout sample of scored records not used in model training.
Join the sample to the demographic/proxy reference table under the approved data-sharing agreement.
Confirm minimum subgroup sample sizes meet statistical power requirements (commonly n≥30 per subgroup); flag under-powered subgroups.
Store the assembled dataset in the model's test workspace with an access log.
checklist.done: the holdout dataset is assembled, demographically labelled and subgroup sample sizes are checked for power.

checklist.step: Run the disparate-impact test battery
actions: In the Azure ML fairness-testing notebook, load the registered MLflow model version and score the holdout dataset.
Compute the adverse impact ratio, demographic parity gap and equal opportunity difference for each protected-characteristic proxy.
Log all metric outputs as MLflow run artefacts tagged to the Model ID and test date.
Flag any subgroup breaching the 0.80 adverse impact ratio threshold.
checklist.done: all fairness metrics are computed, logged as MLflow artefacts and threshold breaches are flagged.

checklist.step: Interpret results and draft the fairness test report
actions: Review the metric outputs against the pass/fail thresholds in the Model Fairness Testing Standard.
Draft the fairness test report: methodology, dataset, metrics, subgroup results, pass/fail conclusion.
Where a subgroup fails, identify the likely driving feature(s) using SHAP or equivalent feature-attribution output.
Attach the report and metric artefacts to the model's record in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the report states a pass/fail conclusion per subgroup with driving-feature analysis for any failure.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate any failing model
actions: Open a GRC exception for any subgroup fail, naming the Model ID, proxy and adverse impact ratio.
Convene the model owner and Data Scientist to select a remediation path: feature removal, re-weighting, threshold adjustment or model retirement.
Set a remediation deadline; block continued production use of a failing HIGH-tier model beyond 30 days without an approved remediation plan.
Track the remediation to completion in the GRC record.
checklist.done: every failing model has an open, tracked remediation plan or is blocked from production within 30 days.

checklist.step: Re-test after remediation
actions: Re-run the disparate-impact test battery against the remediated model version in Azure ML / MLflow.
Confirm the adverse impact ratio now clears 0.80 for every previously failing subgroup.
Log the re-test as a new MLflow run linked to the remediation GRC record.
Notify the Model Risk Manager to close the exception on a pass.
checklist.done: the remediated model version clears every threshold and the exception is closed on evidence.

checklist.step: Get Chief Risk Officer sign-off before go-live or continued use
actions: Review the fairness test report, and remediation evidence where applicable.
Confirm the report methodology matches the approved Model Fairness Testing Standard.
Sign off in the model governance repository, unlocking go-live or continued production status.
Note any conditions attached to the sign-off (e.g. mandatory 6-month re-test instead of annual).
checklist.done: the model shows a dated CRO sign-off before it goes or remains live.

checklist.step: Notify Compliance and update the AI governance program record
actions: Receive the signed-off fairness test report and log it against the model's compliance record.
Update the AI governance program's fairness-testing tracker with the completion date and next-due date.
Flag any pattern of repeat failures across models sharing a common feature for a wider data-sourcing review.
Include the period's fairness-testing summary in the quarterly compliance report.
checklist.done: the tracker shows the current test status for every HIGH-tier model and any pattern is flagged for review.

checklist.step: Brief the Underwriting and Pricing teams on any threshold change
actions: Where remediation changed a rating factor or eligibility rule, brief the Head of Pricing and Chief Underwriting Officer on the change.
Confirm the change is reflected in the rating engine and underwriting guidelines documentation.
Record the briefing date and attendees in the model's change log.
Confirm no parallel, unremediated version of the model remains live in any rating engine environment.
checklist.done: Pricing and Underwriting confirm the remediated logic is the only version live in production.

checklist.step: Review the proxy-variable mapping annually against Equality Act guidance
actions: Review Equality Act 2010 case law and EHRC guidance updates annually for new recognised proxy variables.
Compare against the current approved proxy-variable mapping used in fairness testing.
Recommend additions or removals to the Data Science Lead.
Approve the updated mapping for the next testing cycle.
checklist.done: the proxy-variable mapping is reviewed and re-approved annually against current legal guidance.

checklist.step: Maintain the fairness-testing calendar
actions: Maintain the master calendar of fairness-test due dates per HIGH-tier model in the model governance repository.
Adjust due dates automatically on any logged retrain event.
Send a monthly digest of upcoming and overdue tests to Data Science Lead and Compliance Officer.
Reconcile the calendar to the model inventory quarterly to catch any newly HIGH-tier model.
checklist.done: the calendar is current, reconciled quarterly and drives the monthly digest without gaps.

checklist.step: Document testing limitations and data gaps
actions: Where demographic labels are unavailable or inferred (e.g. no direct ethnicity field), document the inference method and its known error rate.
State any subgroup excluded from testing due to insufficient sample size and the plan to close the gap.
Attach the limitations statement to the fairness test report.
Flag material limitations to the Data Science Lead for disclosure in the sign-off request.
checklist.done: every limitation and data gap is documented and disclosed alongside the test conclusion.

checklist.step: Archive the fairness test evidence pack
actions: Assemble the dataset description, MLflow run artefacts, report, remediation record and CRO sign-off into a single evidence pack per Model ID and test date.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository with the 6-year retention label applied.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by Model ID and test date.
Notify the Model Risk Analyst that the calendar entry can be marked complete.
checklist.done: the evidence pack is filed, labelled for retention and retrievable, and the calendar entry is closed.

checklist.step: Report fairness-testing outcomes to the AI Governance Committee
actions: Compile the quarter's fairness-test pass/fail summary across all HIGH-tier models.
Present trend data (repeat failures, remediation turnaround time) to the AI Governance Committee.
Record committee feedback and any required policy change in the minutes.
Distribute the summary to the Chief Risk Officer and Compliance.
checklist.done: the committee has reviewed and minuted the quarter's fairness-testing summary.

testing.step: Build the population of models due for fairness testing
actions: Extract every HIGH-tier model from the model governance repository with its last fairness-test date.
Identify all models due or overdue in the test period, plus any that went live without a pre-go-live test.
Reconcile the extract to the fairness-testing calendar maintained by the Model Risk Analyst.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the testing calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of models with a failed or overdue-by-more-than-30-days test status.
Take 10 randomly selected passing models (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every overdue or failed model.

testing.step: Re-perform the disparate-impact calculation for each sampled model
actions: Pull the same holdout dataset and MLflow model version referenced in the original fairness test report.
Independently recompute the adverse impact ratio and demographic parity gap for each protected-characteristic proxy.
Compare the recomputed values to the reported values; any material difference is an exception.
Capture the recomputation notebook output into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled model has an independent recomputation with any material difference logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the proxy-variable list used matches the approved mapping
actions: Compare the proxy variables tested in the sampled reports to the current General-Counsel-approved mapping.
Flag any report that used an outdated or incomplete proxy list.
Confirm the mapping in use was the one in force on the test date, not the current one, where the mapping has since changed.
Record findings by Model ID.
testing.done: the proxy list used in each sampled report matches the mapping approved as of that test date.

testing.step: Trace failing models to a completed remediation and re-test
actions: For every sampled model that originally failed, pull the GRC exception record.
Confirm a remediation was implemented, re-tested, and passed before the model resumed or continued production use.
Check the elapsed time between failure and remediation against the 30-day production-block rule for HIGH-tier models.
Flag any model that remained live beyond 30 days without an approved remediation plan as a compliance breach.
testing.done: every sampled failure traces to a timely, evidenced remediation and re-test, or is logged as a breach.

testing.step: Confirm sample-size adequacy and data-gap disclosures
actions: Check the subgroup sample sizes recorded in each sampled report against the stated statistical power requirement.
Confirm any demographic-inference method or excluded subgroup was disclosed in the limitations statement.
Flag any report presenting a conclusion on an under-powered subgroup without disclosure.
Record findings by Model ID.
testing.done: every sampled report's sample-size adequacy and disclosed limitations are independently verified.

testing.step: Verify Chief Risk Officer sign-off exists and pre-dates go-live/continued use
actions: Confirm a dated CRO sign-off exists in the model governance repository for every sampled model.
Compare the sign-off date to the model's go-live date or, for existing models, to the annual due date.
Flag any model used in production before its sign-off date as a control breach.
Capture the sign-off record into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled model shows a CRO sign-off that pre-dates its go-live or continued-use date, or the gap is logged as a breach.

testing.step: Check Pricing and Underwriting adoption of remediated logic
actions: For remediated models affecting rating or eligibility, confirm with the Head of Pricing that only the remediated version is live in the rating engine.
Spot-check a small number of live quotes to confirm the rating factors match the remediated model output.
Flag any evidence of the pre-remediation version still being used.
Record findings by Model ID.
testing.done: no sampled remediated model shows evidence of the pre-remediation version still in live use.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the Model ID, what was missed and the fairness/compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (stale proxy list, under-powered subgroup, late remediation, missing sign-off) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next year's mandatory retest.
Confirm prior-year exceptions were genuinely closed before marking them resolved.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest status.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for HIGH-tier models used beyond 30 days without remediation.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who ran none of the sampled original tests, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the AI Governance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Maintain the master inventory of required AI governance policies
actions: In the GRC platform policy library, list every required AI governance document: model risk policy, fairness-testing standard, human-oversight standard, explainability standard, third-party AI due diligence policy, incident-response addendum.
For each, record the owner, current version, approval date and next-review date.
Compare against the FCA's current AI-related expectations (SYSC 4, PRIN 2A, PROD 4.2, relevant portfolio letters) to confirm no required document is missing.
Flag any missing document and assign a drafting owner.
checklist.done: the inventory lists every required policy with an owner, version and review date, with no missing document unassigned.

checklist.step: Draft or revise a policy ahead of its review date
actions: Pull the current approved version and mark up changes against the latest FCA guidance, internal incident learnings and model inventory scope changes.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Data Officer, Chief Risk Officer and Head of Compliance for comment.
Log all comments and resolutions in the policy's revision history.
Finalise the clean version for approval routing.
checklist.done: the revised draft incorporates reviewer comments and carries a complete revision history.

checklist.step: Route the policy through the approval chain
actions: Review the finalised draft for legal and regulatory sufficiency against current FCA Handbook provisions.
Confirm the policy assigns clear accountable owners for each control it describes.
Route to the Chief Risk Officer for risk sign-off, then to the Board Risk Committee for approval.
Record each approval step with name, role and date in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: the policy shows a complete, dated approval chain ending in Board Risk Committee sign-off.

checklist.step: Publish the approved policy and version-control it
actions: Upload the Board-approved policy to the GRC platform policy library, incrementing the version number.
Supersede the prior version and move it to the archive with its full history intact.
Publish the policy to the compliance intranet and notify all named policy stakeholders.
Set the next annual review date in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: the new version is published, the prior version archived, and the next review date is scheduled.

checklist.step: Collect attestations from accountable owners
actions: Issue an attestation task in the GRC platform to every role named as an accountable owner in the policy (CDO, Data Science Lead, Model Risk Manager, etc.).
Require each to confirm they have read the current version and understand their obligations.
Chase outstanding attestations weekly until 100% complete.
File the completed attestation log against the policy version.
checklist.done: 100% of named accountable owners have a dated attestation on file against the current version.

checklist.step: Map each policy control to the model governance and fairness-testing workflows
actions: Confirm every control described in the policy suite has a corresponding step in the model inventory and fairness-testing procedures.
Identify any policy requirement with no operational workflow behind it and raise a gap ticket.
Update the workflow documentation to close confirmed gaps.
Record the control-to-workflow mapping for audit reference.
checklist.done: every policy control maps to an operating workflow, with gaps ticketed and tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Monitor for FCA publications that trigger an off-cycle review
actions: Subscribe to FCA publications (discussion papers, policy statements, portfolio letters) relevant to AI and Consumer Duty.
On any relevant publication, assess within 10 business days whether it triggers an off-cycle policy review.
Where triggered, notify the Compliance Officer and set a 90-day off-cycle review deadline.
Log the assessment and its outcome in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every relevant FCA publication has a logged assessment within 10 business days, with off-cycle reviews deadlined at 90 days.

checklist.step: Trigger a policy review after an AI-related incident
actions: On any logged AI-related incident (fairness-test failure left unremediated, model outage causing customer harm, data breach involving a model), assess whether the relevant policy needs revision.
Document the incident's root cause and whether it reflects a policy gap versus an execution failure.
Where a policy gap is found, trigger the drafting step with a 90-day deadline.
Record the incident-to-policy-review linkage in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every AI-related incident has a documented policy-gap assessment, with confirmed gaps triggering a 90-day review.

checklist.step: Review the third-party AI due diligence policy against the vendor register
actions: Confirm the current third-party AI due diligence policy's requirements are reflected in the vendor onboarding checklist.
Spot-check three recently onboarded AI vendors against the checklist for completeness.
Flag any checklist item the policy requires but onboarding does not currently capture.
Feed findings into the next policy revision cycle.
checklist.done: the vendor onboarding checklist is confirmed aligned to the current policy, with gaps fed into the next revision.

checklist.step: Present the annual governance program assurance report to the Board
actions: Compile the year's policy review status, attestation completion rate, incident-triggered reviews and open gaps.
Present the assurance report to the Board Risk Committee.
Record Board feedback and any directed action in the minutes.
Distribute the approved report to Compliance and Internal Audit.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the annual governance assurance report.

checklist.step: Cross-reference the policy suite to related regulatory regimes
actions: Confirm the AI governance policy suite cross-references UK GDPR, the Equality Act 2010 and any sector-specific PRA expectations that also apply.
Identify any conflicting or duplicated requirement across regimes and resolve with the accountable owners.
Update the policy's regulatory-basis section with the confirmed cross-references.
Record the review date and outcome.
checklist.done: the policy suite's regulatory-basis section is current and free of unresolved cross-regime conflicts.

checklist.step: Escalate lapsed policies immediately
actions: Run the GRC platform's lapsed-policy report identifying any document past its review date.
Issue an interim-effectiveness statement confirming the prior version remains the operative control pending re-approval.
Escalate to the Chief Risk Officer for sign-off on the interim statement within 5 business days.
Prioritise the lapsed policy's re-approval ahead of all other queued reviews.
checklist.done: every lapsed policy has a signed interim-effectiveness statement within 5 business days and a prioritised re-approval track.

checklist.step: Train accountable owners on policy changes
actions: On publication of a materially revised policy, build or update the corresponding training module in the learning management system.
Assign the module to every accountable owner and their direct reports.
Track completion and chase non-completion after 15 business days.
Report completion rates to the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: training is assigned within 10 business days of publication and completion is tracked to at least 95%.

checklist.step: Reconcile the policy suite to the model inventory scope
actions: Compare the model types and decision uses named in the policy suite to the current model inventory categories.
Identify any inventory category (e.g. a newly added generative-AI use case) not addressed by an existing policy.
Raise a drafting request for any uncovered category.
Record the reconciliation outcome quarterly.
checklist.done: every model inventory category maps to a governing policy, with gaps raised as drafting requests.

checklist.step: Retain the policy and attestation evidence
actions: File each policy version, approval chain, attestation log and Board minute into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by policy name and version.
Verify the prior year's evidence remains retrievable before closing the current cycle.
checklist.done: the year's policy governance evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by policy name.

testing.step: Build the population of policies in force during the period
actions: Extract the full policy library from the GRC platform with version, approval date and review-due date.
Reconcile the extract to the master policy inventory maintained by the Compliance Officer.
Identify any policy referenced in operating procedures but absent from the library.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the master inventory and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of policies past their review date at any point in the test period.
Take 5 randomly selected on-time policies (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every lapsed policy.

testing.step: Re-verify the approval chain for each sampled policy
actions: Confirm each approval step (drafting reviewer, General Counsel, Chief Risk Officer, Board Risk Committee) is present with name, role and date.
Cross-check the Board Risk Committee approval against the actual committee minutes.
Flag any policy published without a matching minuted Board approval.
Capture the minute excerpt into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled policy's approval chain is independently confirmed against committee minutes.

testing.step: Verify attestation completeness on the sample
actions: Pull the attestation log for each sampled policy and list every named accountable owner.
Confirm 100% of named owners have a dated attestation against the current version.
Flag any owner with no attestation or an attestation against a superseded version.
Record findings by policy name.
testing.done: attestation completeness is independently confirmed for every sampled policy, with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Test whether lapsed policies had a timely interim-effectiveness statement
actions: For each sampled lapsed policy, confirm an interim-effectiveness statement was issued within 5 business days of the lapse.
Confirm the Chief Risk Officer signed the interim statement.
Flag any lapse with no interim statement, or one issued late, as an exception.
Record the lapse duration in days for each finding.
testing.done: every sampled lapse either has a timely, signed interim statement or is logged as an exception with its duration.

testing.step: Verify control-to-workflow mapping on the sample
actions: For each sampled policy, pick two stated controls and confirm an operating workflow step actually implements each one.
Interview the relevant workflow owner (e.g. Model Risk Manager, Data Science Lead) to confirm the control is genuinely performed, not just documented.
Flag any control with no corresponding live workflow as a design gap.
Record findings by policy and control.
testing.done: each sampled policy's tested controls are confirmed operating in practice, or gaps are flagged.

testing.step: Confirm off-cycle review triggers were acted on
actions: Pull the log of FCA publications and AI incidents assessed for off-cycle review triggers during the period.
Confirm each trigger assessment was made within the 10-business-day requirement.
For any confirmed trigger, confirm the resulting review completed within the 90-day deadline.
Flag any missed assessment or overdue off-cycle review.
testing.done: every trigger event has a timely logged assessment and, where triggered, a review completed within 90 days.

testing.step: Check training completion evidence on the sample
actions: For each sampled materially revised policy, pull the training completion report from the learning management system.
Confirm completion reached at least 95% within the tracked window.
Flag any policy with lower completion or no training module created.
Record findings by policy name.
testing.done: training completion is independently verified against the 95% target for every sampled revised policy.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the policy name, what was missed and the governance impact.
Assign a root cause (late review, missing attestation, workflow gap, missed trigger) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next year's mandatory retest.
Confirm prior-year exceptions were genuinely closed before marking them resolved.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest status.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 30-day lapse threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted or approved none of the sampled policies, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and Board reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm documentation is required before build begins
actions: On any model classified HIGH-tier in the inventory, open the Model Documentation record in the model governance repository.
Set the record status to 'Documentation Required — Not Started' and link it to the model's inventory ID.
Assign the documentation owner (the model's lead Data Scientist).
Set the target completion date ahead of the planned go-live date.
checklist.done: every HIGH-tier model has an open, assigned documentation record before build sign-off.

checklist.step: Write the decision-logic summary in plain language
actions: Describe in plain, non-technical language what the model predicts, its main inputs and how the output feeds the business decision.
Avoid unexplained jargon; where a technical term is unavoidable, define it in a glossary section.
Have a colleague outside the build team read the summary and confirm they understand the decision logic without further explanation.
Attach the reviewed summary to the documentation record.
checklist.done: the plain-language summary passes an outside-reader comprehension check and is attached to the record.

checklist.step: Generate the explainability artefact
actions: In Azure ML, run the approved explainability method (SHAP for tree/ensemble models, LIME or integrated gradients for other model classes) against a representative sample of scored records.
Log the global feature-importance chart and at least 5 individual-record explanation examples as MLflow artefacts.
Confirm the top contributing features align with the plain-language decision-logic summary; investigate and resolve any mismatch.
Attach the explainability artefacts to the documentation record.
checklist.done: explainability artefacts are generated, logged in MLflow and reconciled to the plain-language summary.

checklist.step: Design and name the human-override role
actions: Identify the named role empowered to review, question or override the model's output before it acts on a customer (e.g. Senior Underwriter for pricing overrides, Claims Examiner for triage overrides).
Document the override role's authority, the trigger conditions for review and the escalation path if the override role disagrees with the model.
Confirm the override role has received training on the model's decision logic and its limitations.
Record the override design and named role in the documentation record.
checklist.done: a named, trained override role and escalation path is documented for the model.

checklist.step: Draft the customer-facing explanation template
actions: Draft a plain-English explanation template a customer can request or receive, describing the factors that influenced their pricing, underwriting or claims decision.
Confirm the template meets UK GDPR Article 13/14 transparency requirements and does not disclose commercially sensitive model internals.
Route the template through Compliance for Consumer Duty (fair-value communication) review.
Attach the approved template to the documentation record.
checklist.done: the customer-facing explanation template is approved and attached to the documentation record.

checklist.step: Test the explanation template against a real scored record
actions: Populate the approved template using the explainability output for a real (anonymised) scored record.
Confirm the populated explanation is coherent, accurate and does not contradict the model's actual decision logic.
Have the Legal Counsel review the populated example for compliance and clarity.
Attach the tested example to the documentation record.
checklist.done: a populated, reviewed example explanation is attached and confirmed coherent with the model's actual logic.

checklist.step: Route the documentation package for CDO sign-off
actions: Review the completed decision-logic summary, explainability artefacts, override design and explanation template together.
Confirm every required section of the Model Documentation Standard is present and internally consistent.
Sign off and set the documentation record status to 'Complete'.
Confirm the model's go-live gate in the inventory is unblocked only after this sign-off.
checklist.done: the documentation record is marked 'Complete' with a dated CDO sign-off before go-live.

checklist.step: Refresh documentation on material model change
actions: On any retrain, feature-set change or override-design change, reopen the documentation record.
Re-run the explainability artefact generation and update the decision-logic summary and explanation template as needed.
Route the updated package for CDO re-sign-off within 10 business days of the change going live.
Version the documentation record to match the model version.
checklist.done: documentation is refreshed and re-signed within 10 business days of any material model change.

checklist.step: Train the override role on the current documentation
actions: Build or update the training module covering the model's decision logic, the override role's authority and the escalation path.
Assign the module to every individual holding the named override role.
Track completion and confirm 100% completion before the model or its update goes live.
Report completion status to the Chief Data Officer.
checklist.done: 100% of override-role holders have completed current training before go-live.

checklist.step: Log and respond to customer explanation requests
actions: Log every customer request for an explanation of an AI-influenced decision in the case-management system.
Pull the approved explanation template and populate it using the record's actual explainability output.
Route the populated explanation through Legal Counsel review before sending where the case is a formal complaint.
Respond within the Consumer Duty-aligned service standard (target 10 business days) and log the response date.
checklist.done: every explanation request is logged, populated from real model output and answered within the service standard.

checklist.step: Audit override usage patterns
actions: Pull the override log for each HIGH-tier model quarterly.
Analyse override frequency and reasons; an unusually low override rate may indicate rubber-stamping rather than genuine review.
Flag any override role showing a 0% override rate over a full quarter for a process check.
Report findings to the Chief Data Officer.
checklist.done: override usage is reviewed quarterly and any suspiciously low override rate is flagged and investigated.

checklist.step: Reconcile documentation status to the model inventory
actions: Run a monthly report of HIGH-tier models in 'In Production' status against documentation records marked 'Complete'.
Flag any production model with an incomplete or missing documentation record.
Escalate flagged models to the Chief Data Officer for immediate remediation.
Record the reconciliation outcome each month.
checklist.done: no HIGH-tier production model shows an incomplete documentation record beyond the current month's reconciliation.

checklist.step: Escalate undocumented HIGH-tier models
actions: Open a GRC exception for any HIGH-tier model found live without complete documentation.
Require the Chief Data Officer to complete and sign off documentation within 15 business days.
Escalate to the Chief Risk Officer if the deadline is missed.
Close the exception only on confirmed sign-off.
checklist.done: every undocumented HIGH-tier model has a tracked GRC exception closed within 15 business days or escalated.

checklist.step: Review explainability method suitability annually
actions: Annually review whether the explainability method used (SHAP, LIME, etc.) remains appropriate for the current model architecture.
Where a model has moved to a new architecture (e.g. gradient boosting to a neural network), confirm the explainability method still produces valid, stable explanations.
Update the Model Documentation Standard's approved-methods list if needed.
Notify affected model owners of any required documentation refresh.
checklist.done: explainability method suitability is reviewed annually with any required refresh notified to model owners.

checklist.step: Retain the documentation evidence
actions: File each model's documentation package (summary, explainability artefacts, override design, explanation template, sign-off) into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year-from-decommission retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by Model ID.
Verify prior versions remain retrievable alongside the current one.
checklist.done: the documentation package is filed, labelled for 6-year retention and retrievable by Model ID.

testing.step: Build the population of HIGH-tier models requiring documentation
actions: Extract every HIGH-tier model from the model governance repository with its documentation record status.
Reconcile the extract to the model inventory's production status list.
Identify any HIGH-tier production model with no matching documentation record.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the inventory and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of models with an incomplete or missing documentation record.
Take 10 randomly selected models with a 'Complete' record (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every incomplete-documentation model.

testing.step: Re-verify the explainability artefact for each sampled model
actions: Open the logged MLflow explainability run for the sampled model and confirm it corresponds to the current live model version.
Independently review whether the top contributing features are consistent with the documented decision-logic summary.
Flag any mismatch or any artefact generated against a superseded model version.
Capture the artefact review notes into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled model's explainability artefact is independently confirmed current and consistent with its documentation.

testing.step: Confirm the named override role is real and trained
actions: Confirm the named override role in the documentation is held by a current employee in that role.
Pull the training completion record for that individual and confirm it is current.
Interview the override-role holder to confirm they understand their authority and the escalation path.
Flag any gap between documented and actual practice.
testing.done: the override role is confirmed real, trained and understood for every sampled model.

testing.step: Test the customer-facing explanation template against a real record
actions: Independently populate the approved template using a different (anonymised) scored record than the one used at documentation time.
Confirm the resulting explanation is coherent, accurate and meets UK GDPR transparency requirements.
Flag any template that produces an inconsistent or non-compliant explanation on re-test.
Record findings by Model ID.
testing.done: the explanation template is independently re-tested against a fresh record for every sampled model.

testing.step: Trace a sample of logged customer explanation requests to timely, accurate responses
actions: Pull 10 logged customer explanation requests from the case-management system across the test period.
Confirm each was answered within the 10-business-day service standard using the approved template and real model output.
Confirm any formal complaint case received Legal Counsel review before the response was sent.
Flag any late, generic or unreviewed response as an exception.
testing.done: the sampled explanation requests are confirmed answered on time, accurately and with required legal review.

testing.step: Recompute override usage rates and investigate anomalies
actions: Independently recompute the override rate for each sampled model's override role over the test period.
Compare to the rate reported in the quarterly override-usage review.
Investigate any override role showing a 0% rate not already flagged and interview the role holder.
Record findings by Model ID and role.
testing.done: override rates are independently recomputed and any unflagged anomaly is investigated.

testing.step: Verify material-change refresh timeliness
actions: For sampled models with a logged retrain or feature-set change in the period, confirm the documentation refresh and re-sign-off occurred within 10 business days.
Flag any refresh completed late or not at all.
Cross-check the change log timestamp against the documentation record's version history.
Record findings by Model ID.
testing.done: documentation refresh timeliness is independently confirmed for every sampled changed model.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the Model ID, what was missed and the governance impact.
Assign a root cause (stale artefact, untrained override role, non-compliant template, late refresh) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next year's mandatory retest.
Confirm prior-year exceptions were genuinely closed before marking them resolved.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest status.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missing override roles or explainability artefacts.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled documentation, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the AI Governance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Intake and triage the FCA inquiry on receipt
actions: On receipt of any FCA letter, portfolio-letter follow-up, section 165 request or attestation request touching AI, log it in the regulatory inquiry tracker within 1 business day.
Record the request's exact scope, the named FCA contact, any stated deadline and the request reference number.
Classify the request type (information request, attestation, thematic review, section 165 notice).
Assign a response owner and notify General Counsel and Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the inquiry is logged within 1 business day with scope, deadline and an assigned owner.

checklist.step: Determine the statutory or interpreted response deadline
actions: Where the FCA letter states an explicit deadline, record it verbatim in the tracker.
Where no explicit deadline is given, apply the firm's 10-business-day reasonable-time standard and record the computed date.
Confirm whether the request falls under formal section 165 FSMA powers, which carries statutory compulsion, versus an informal request.
Set the tracker's deadline field and flag section 165 requests as high-priority.
checklist.done: every inquiry carries a confirmed deadline and a correct classification of its statutory basis.

checklist.step: Scope the evidence required and assign gathering tasks
actions: Break the request into discrete evidence items (e.g. model inventory extract, fairness-test reports, governance policy versions, override logs).
Assign each item to the accountable data owner (Chief Data Officer, Data Science Lead, Model Risk Manager) with an internal sub-deadline at least 5 business days before the external deadline.
Track sub-task completion daily in the tracker.
Escalate any sub-task at risk of missing its internal deadline to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every evidence item has an assigned owner and an internal sub-deadline ahead of the external deadline.

checklist.step: Pull evidence from the model governance repository and GRC platform
actions: Export the requested model inventory records, fairness-test reports and documentation packages exactly matching the request's stated scope and date range.
Verify the export is complete by cross-checking record counts against the live inventory.
Redact any information outside the request's scope or containing unrelated personal data.
Hand the evidence package to the Compliance Officer with a completeness confirmation.
checklist.done: the evidence package matches the request scope exactly, is verified complete and is confirmed as handed over.

checklist.step: Draft the narrative response
actions: Draft a narrative response addressing each question or requirement in the FCA letter point by point.
Reference the specific evidence exhibit supporting each statement.
Avoid speculative or unsupported claims; where information is not available, state that explicitly with the reason.
Circulate the draft to the response owner and Chief Data Officer for factual accuracy review.
checklist.done: the draft answers every point in the letter, each referencing a specific evidence exhibit, with no unsupported claims.

checklist.step: Route the draft through legal review
actions: Review the narrative response and evidence pack for legal accuracy, privilege issues and consistency with prior FCA submissions.
Flag any statement that could be read as an admission of a control failure and confirm it is accurate and necessary.
Require correction of any inaccurate or inconsistent statement before proceeding.
Provide written sign-off in the tracker once satisfied.
checklist.done: General Counsel has signed off the response as legally accurate and consistent with prior submissions.

checklist.step: Obtain Head of Compliance final approval
actions: Present the final response package to the Head of Compliance for approval.
Confirm the response has been reviewed by every accountable data owner named in it.
Record the approval with name, role and date in the tracker.
Prepare the submission in the format and channel specified by the FCA (letter, portal, email to the named supervisor).
checklist.done: the Head of Compliance has approved the final package and the submission format matches the FCA's specified channel.

checklist.step: Submit the response before the deadline
actions: Submit the response through the specified channel at least 1 business day ahead of the deadline where feasible.
Retain the submission confirmation (delivery receipt, sent email, portal confirmation) as evidence.
Log the actual submission date and time in the tracker.
Notify the Head of Compliance and General Counsel that submission is complete.
checklist.done: the response is submitted on or ahead of the deadline with retained submission confirmation.

checklist.step: Log and file the FCA's acknowledgement or follow-up
actions: On receipt of any FCA acknowledgement, follow-up question or closure notice, log it against the original inquiry record.
If a follow-up question is received, restart the triage step for the follow-up as a linked sub-inquiry.
Close the original inquiry record only once the FCA has confirmed no further information is required.
File all correspondence chronologically against the inquiry record.
checklist.done: the inquiry record shows every piece of correspondence and is only closed on FCA confirmation.

checklist.step: Debrief internally on lessons from the inquiry
actions: Convene a short debrief with the response owner, Chief Data Officer and General Counsel after closure.
Identify any evidence gap, process delay or documentation weakness the inquiry exposed.
Raise action items against the AI governance program (policy, inventory or documentation improvements) as needed.
Record the debrief outcome in the tracker.
checklist.done: every closed inquiry has a documented debrief with any resulting action items raised.

checklist.step: Maintain the standing evidence-readiness pack
actions: Maintain a continuously current export-ready evidence pack (model inventory summary, fairness-test status, governance policy index) so it can be pulled within 24 hours of any inquiry.
Refresh the standing pack monthly regardless of whether an inquiry is open.
Confirm the pack's completeness with Compliance quarterly.
Store the current pack in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a current, complete standing evidence pack exists and is refreshed at least monthly.

checklist.step: Track cumulative inquiry themes across the year
actions: Tag each closed inquiry by theme (model risk, fairness, explainability, notices, incident-related).
Compile a quarterly theme report showing frequency and any recurring FCA concern.
Present recurring themes to the AI Governance Committee for a proactive control response.
Update the FCA Inquiry Response Procedure if a systemic weakness is identified.
checklist.done: recurring inquiry themes are identified quarterly and fed back into governance improvements.

checklist.step: Verify the named FCA contact and escalation path are current
actions: Confirm annually that the firm's named supervisory contact at the FCA and internal escalation contacts are current.
Update the FCA Inquiry Response Procedure with any change.
Notify all response owners of the current contact details.
Record the confirmation date.
checklist.done: the named FCA contact and internal escalation path are confirmed current at least annually.

checklist.step: Rehearse a mock inquiry response annually
actions: Run an annual tabletop exercise simulating a section 165 AI-related information request.
Time the evidence-gathering and drafting steps against the internal sub-deadlines.
Identify any bottleneck (slow evidence pull, unclear ownership) and remediate before the next cycle.
Record the exercise outcome and remediation actions.
checklist.done: an annual mock inquiry exercise is completed with documented bottlenecks and remediation actions.

checklist.step: Retain the full inquiry evidence trail
actions: File the inquiry, all evidence exhibits, the approved response, submission confirmation and FCA acknowledgement together.
Apply the 7-year-from-submission retention label in the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by FCA request reference number.
Verify closed prior-year inquiries remain retrievable.
checklist.done: the inquiry trail is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by request reference number.

testing.step: Build the population of FCA inquiries logged in the period
actions: Extract every inquiry record from the regulatory inquiry tracker logged in the test period.
Reconcile the extract to correspondence held by Head of Compliance and General Counsel's mailboxes for any inquiry not logged.
List any unlogged inquiry found as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled against correspondence and signed as complete, with unlogged inquiries flagged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of section 165 statutory requests.
Take 5 randomly selected informal requests (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every section 165 request.

testing.step: Verify deadline determination and internal sub-deadlines
actions: For each sampled inquiry, confirm the recorded deadline matches the FCA letter's stated date, or the 10-business-day standard where none was stated.
Confirm internal sub-deadlines were set at least 5 business days ahead of the external deadline.
Flag any inquiry with no recorded sub-deadlines or a miscalculated external deadline.
Record findings by inquiry reference.
testing.done: deadline determination and sub-deadline setting are independently confirmed for every sampled inquiry.

testing.step: Trace evidence exhibits back to source systems
actions: For each sampled inquiry, pull the evidence exhibits referenced in the final response.
Re-generate the equivalent extract from the model governance repository or GRC platform and compare to the submitted exhibit.
Flag any exhibit that does not match a re-generated extract or appears incomplete against the request's scope.
Capture the comparison into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled response's evidence exhibits are independently traced and confirmed accurate.

testing.step: Confirm General Counsel and Head of Compliance sign-off exist and pre-date submission
actions: Confirm both sign-offs are present in the tracker for each sampled inquiry.
Compare the sign-off dates to the actual submission date and time.
Flag any response submitted before both sign-offs were recorded.
Record findings by inquiry reference.
testing.done: both required sign-offs are confirmed present and pre-dating submission for every sampled inquiry.

testing.step: Recompute submission timeliness
actions: Compare the logged submission date/time to the recorded deadline for each sampled inquiry.
Flag any submission after the deadline as a fail, including submissions made on the deadline day after the FCA's stated cut-off time.
Cross-check the retained submission confirmation (receipt, sent email, portal confirmation) against the logged date.
Record findings by inquiry reference.
testing.done: submission timeliness is independently recomputed and confirmed against retained confirmations for every sampled inquiry.

testing.step: Verify closure only occurred on FCA confirmation
actions: For each sampled closed inquiry, confirm a logged FCA acknowledgement or closure notice exists.
Flag any inquiry closed internally with no corresponding FCA confirmation on file.
Confirm any follow-up question was tracked as a linked sub-inquiry rather than ignored.
Record findings by inquiry reference.
testing.done: closure is independently confirmed as evidenced by an FCA confirmation for every sampled inquiry.

testing.step: Check the debrief and standing evidence pack currency
actions: Confirm a debrief record exists for each sampled closed inquiry.
Pull the current standing evidence-readiness pack and confirm its last-refreshed date is within the past month.
Flag a stale standing pack or a missing debrief as a process exception.
Record findings.
testing.done: debrief completion and standing-pack currency are independently confirmed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the inquiry reference, what was missed and the regulatory impact.
Assign a root cause (unlogged inquiry, missed deadline, unverified exhibit, missing sign-off) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed statutory deadline, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next year's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missed-statutory-deadline threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and Board reporting date exists in the repository.
