checklist.step: Identify every decision type where an AI model materially influences the outcome
actions: Query the model governance repository for HIGH-tier models by decision type: application pricing, underwriting decline, renewal repricing, claims-triage outcome.
For each decision type, confirm whether the model output is the sole driver, a material input alongside human judgement, or advisory only.
Hand the classified list to the Insurance Product Manager and General Counsel.
Flag any newly identified decision type since the last review for immediate notice-gap assessment.
checklist.done: a current, classified list of AI-influenced decision types exists and has been handed to Product and Legal.

checklist.step: Draft the required notice text per decision type
actions: For each AI-influenced decision type, draft notice text meeting UK GDPR Article 13/14 transparency requirements and FCA Consumer Duty plain-language expectations.
State clearly that automated processing is used, what it assesses, and how the customer can request human review or an explanation.
Run the draft through a plain-language / readability check appropriate for retail customers.
Version and date the approved notice text in the notice text library.
checklist.done: approved, versioned notice text exists for every AI-influenced decision type and passes the readability check.

checklist.step: Map notice text to the specific forms and correspondence templates
actions: List every form and correspondence template affected by each decision type: quote/application form, decline letter, renewal notice, claims-decision letter.
For each template, specify exact placement (e.g. footer of the quote page, opening paragraph of a decline letter) per the Product Notices and Disclosures Standard.
Build the mapping table linking decision type, notice version and template ID.
Hand the mapping to the Policy Forms Specialist for build.
checklist.done: a complete decision-type-to-template mapping with specified placement exists for every affected form.

checklist.step: Embed the notice as a managed content block in the policy administration system
actions: In the policy administration system's correspondence template designer, create or update the managed content block holding the approved notice text.
Insert the content block at the specified placement in each mapped template, using the template's merge-field engine rather than hard-coded text.
Set the content block's effective date to align with the triggering product or process change's go-live date.
Save as a draft version pending compliance review.
checklist.done: the notice content block is embedded at the correct placement in every mapped template as a dated draft.

checklist.step: Generate a proof document for each updated template
actions: Run a test-case merge through the policy administration system for each updated template using representative dummy customer data.
Generate a PDF proof showing the notice text rendered in its actual placement and font.
Confirm no merge-field errors or truncated text.
Attach the proof to the form's build record.
checklist.done: a clean PDF proof exists for every updated template showing the notice correctly rendered.

checklist.step: Route the proof for Compliance and Legal review
actions: Review each proof against the approved notice text and placement rules in the Product Notices and Disclosures Standard.
Confirm the notice is not buried in fine print or contradicted by other template language.
Route to General Counsel for final legal sign-off.
Record the review outcome in the form's build record.
checklist.done: every updated template's proof is reviewed by Compliance and signed off by General Counsel before release.

checklist.step: Promote the reviewed template to production ahead of the triggering change
actions: Promote the signed-off template version from the test environment to production in the policy administration system.
Confirm the go-live date is set to align with or precede the triggering product/process change's effective date.
Run a final smoke test generating a live-environment proof document.
Close the form's build record as 'Released'.
checklist.done: the template is live in production with a smoke-tested proof, released no later than the triggering change's effective date.

checklist.step: Update the form inventory register
actions: Add or update the entry in the form inventory: form ID, decision type, notice version, placement, release date, sign-off references.
Retire and archive any superseded template version, retaining its history.
Confirm the inventory is the single source of truth queried by the compliance testing process.
Notify Compliance that the inventory has been updated.
checklist.done: the form inventory reflects the current released version with full version history retained.

checklist.step: Confirm the release gate blocked go-live without a notice review
actions: Check the product change tracker for the triggering change and confirm the notice-review task shows 'Complete' before go-live status was set.
Where the gate was bypassed, immediately assess whether the live product is now non-compliant.
Escalate any bypass to the Head of Compliance and open a remediation ticket.
Record the gate-check outcome.
checklist.done: the release gate is confirmed to have blocked go-live until the notice review was complete, or a bypass is escalated and remediated.

checklist.step: Train customer-facing teams on the new notice content
actions: Update training materials for Underwriting, Claims and Customer Service teams to reflect the new notice text and its purpose.
Assign the update to relevant teams and track completion.
Prepare talking points for staff fielding customer questions about the automated-decision notice.
Report completion to the Insurance Product Manager.
checklist.done: customer-facing teams are trained on the new notice content before or immediately after release.

checklist.step: Monitor complaint volumes for notice-related confusion
actions: Tag complaints referencing confusion about automated decisions or requests for human review.
Compile a monthly volume trend and share with the Insurance Product Manager and Legal Counsel.
Where a notice appears to be driving confusion, raise a wording-review request.
Record the monitoring outcome each month.
checklist.done: notice-related complaint volume is monitored monthly and any wording concern is fed back for review.

checklist.step: Reconcile the notice inventory to the AI model inventory quarterly
actions: Compare the AI-influenced decision types in the model governance repository to the decision types covered in the notice inventory.
Flag any HIGH-tier model decision type with no corresponding notice mapping.
Route gaps to the Insurance Product Manager for immediate remediation.
Record the reconciliation outcome quarterly.
checklist.done: every HIGH-tier model's decision type maps to a notice, with gaps routed for remediation quarterly.

checklist.step: Review notice text annually against FCA Consumer Duty guidance
actions: Review FCA Consumer Duty and disclosure guidance updates annually.
Compare current notice text against updated guidance for continued adequacy.
Recommend revisions where guidance has moved and route through the drafting step.
Record the annual review outcome.
checklist.done: notice text adequacy is reviewed annually against current FCA guidance with any gap routed for revision.

checklist.step: Escalate a missing-notice finding as a control failure
actions: Raise a tracker issue immediately on discovering any live template missing a required notice.
Assess the number of customers who received the decision without the notice and the exposure window.
Route to General Counsel for a self-report assessment where the exposure is material.
Track remediation of the template and any required customer remediation to closure.
checklist.done: every missing-notice finding is escalated, assessed for exposure and tracked to remediation closure.

checklist.step: Retain the form and notice version evidence
actions: File the form inventory, notice text versions, proofs and sign-offs into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by form ID and decision type.
Verify superseded versions remain retrievable alongside the current one.
checklist.done: the form and notice evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by form ID.

testing.step: Build the population of active AI-influenced templates
actions: Extract every active correspondence template from the policy administration system's template library.
Cross-reference against the model governance repository's list of HIGH-tier AI-influenced decision types.
Identify which templates should carry a notice and reconcile to the form inventory.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population of notice-required templates is reconciled to the model inventory and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of decline and claims-decision templates.
Take 10 randomly selected other templates (quote, renewal) (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every decline and claims-decision template.

testing.step: Generate a live proof for each sampled template
actions: Independently run a test-case merge in the policy administration system for each sampled template.
Generate a fresh PDF proof and visually confirm the notice text is present, at the correct placement and not truncated.
Compare the rendered text word-for-word to the currently approved version in the notice text library.
Capture the proof into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled template's live rendering is independently verified against the approved notice text.

testing.step: Verify placement and prominence against the Standard
actions: Compare each sampled proof's actual notice placement to the rule specified in the Product Notices and Disclosures Standard.
Assess whether the notice is legible and not buried below unrelated boilerplate.
Flag any placement or prominence deviation as an exception.
Record findings by template ID.
testing.done: placement and prominence are independently assessed against the Standard for every sampled template.

testing.step: Confirm legal sign-off exists and pre-dates the release date
actions: Pull the General Counsel sign-off record for each sampled template's current version.
Compare the sign-off date to the template's production go-live date.
Flag any template released before its sign-off date.
Record findings by template ID.
testing.done: legal sign-off is confirmed present and pre-dating release for every sampled template.

testing.step: Trace release timing against the triggering product change
actions: For each sampled template tied to a specific product or process change, pull the change's effective date from the product change tracker.
Confirm the template's notice-carrying version was live on or before that effective date.
Flag any gap where customers could have received the decision before the notice was live.
Record findings by template ID.
testing.done: release timing against the triggering change is independently confirmed for every sampled template.

testing.step: Reconcile the notice inventory to the model inventory
actions: Independently re-run the reconciliation between HIGH-tier AI decision types and the notice inventory.
Confirm every decision type identified in the reconciliation has a live, sampled-and-verified notice.
Flag any decision type with no corresponding notice as a critical exception.
Record findings.
testing.done: the notice-to-model reconciliation is independently re-performed with any gap flagged as critical.

testing.step: Review complaint records for notice-related exposure
actions: Pull complaint records tagged as notice-related for the test period.
Assess whether any complaint reveals a customer receiving an undisclosed automated decision.
Cross-reference the complaint date against the affected template's notice-release date.
Record findings and any exposure identified.
testing.done: complaint records are reviewed for notice-related exposure and any finding is cross-referenced to release timing.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the template ID, what was missed and the customer exposure.
Assign a root cause (build error, late release, placement failure, missing sign-off) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for material customer exposure, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel.
Carry unresolved items into next cycle's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missing notices.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled notice text, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the trigger events are correctly configured
actions: In the policy administration system's business rules engine, locate the event triggers for decline, renewal-repricing and claims-decision outcomes.
Confirm each trigger fires immediately on the decision being finalised in the underwriting or claims workstation, not on a batch delay.
Test-fire each trigger type in the UAT environment and confirm the notice-generation task queues correctly.
Record the confirmed trigger configuration in the change log.
checklist.done: all three trigger types are confirmed firing immediately on decision finalisation in UAT.

checklist.step: Generate the notice from the approved template on trigger
actions: Confirm the automated workflow pulls the current approved notice template (per REG-064-C06's mapping) and merges the customer's actual decision data.
Check the merged notice for correct policy number, decision date and any monetary figures (new premium, decline reason category).
Route any merge exception (missing field, template error) to the Policy Admin Ops Lead same-day rather than allowing a blank or broken notice to queue.
Confirm the generated notice enters the delivery queue with a generation timestamp.
checklist.done: every triggered event produces a correctly merged notice with a logged generation timestamp same-day.

checklist.step: Select and confirm the delivery channel
actions: Check the customer's communication preference on file (post, email, Customer Self-Service Portal message).
Apply the channel priority rule: use the customer's elected preference; default to post where no preference is on file or email has previously bounced.
Confirm the address or email on file was validated within the last 12 months; flag stale contact data for verification before sending.
Set the delivery channel on the notice record.
checklist.done: every notice carries a confirmed, validated delivery channel before dispatch.

checklist.step: Dispatch the notice within its statutory delivery window
actions: Dispatch decline notices within 5 business days of the decision date; renewal-repricing notices at least 21 calendar days before the renewal date; claims-decision notices within 3 business days of the decision.
For portal delivery, publish the notice to the Customer Self-Service Portal and trigger the email/SMS alert that a document is ready.
For post, hand off to the mail house with the required same-day or next-day print SLA.
Log the actual dispatch timestamp against the notice record.
checklist.done: the notice is dispatched inside its statutory window with a logged dispatch timestamp.

checklist.step: Confirm delivery and capture proof
actions: For email/portal delivery, confirm the send-confirmation and (where available) the read/open event from the delivery platform.
For post, confirm the mail house's dispatch confirmation and batch reference.
Attach the delivery proof to the notice log entry.
Where no delivery confirmation is received within 2 business days of dispatch, escalate to check for a bounce or return.
checklist.done: every dispatched notice has an attached delivery proof or an escalated bounce investigation within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Handle bounced or undeliverable notices
actions: On a bounced email or returned-mail notification, open an undeliverable-notice case.
Attempt to verify updated contact details via the CRM and any recent customer contact (claim call, policy service request).
Re-dispatch through the corrected channel within 2 business days of identifying the failure.
If no valid contact can be found, escalate to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for a manual outreach attempt (phone call) and document the attempt.
checklist.done: every bounced notice is re-dispatched within 2 business days of the failure being identified, or escalated with a documented manual attempt.

checklist.step: Log every notice in the Notice Log with full lifecycle timestamps
actions: Record trigger event, generation timestamp, dispatch timestamp, delivery channel and delivery/bounce status for every notice.
Link the log entry to the policy number and the underlying AI decision record in the model governance repository.
Confirm no log entry is left with a blank dispatch or delivery-status field beyond 3 business days of triggering.
Reconcile the log daily against the event trigger count to catch missed generations.
checklist.done: the notice log carries a complete lifecycle record for every triggered event, reconciled daily against trigger counts.

checklist.step: Escalate any notice at risk of missing its statutory window
actions: Monitor the notice log dashboard for any event inside 80% of its delivery window with no dispatch logged.
Contact the assigned Policy Administration Analyst to expedite same-day.
Where the window will be missed regardless, notify the Compliance Officer immediately, not after the fact.
Record the at-risk event and its resolution.
checklist.done: every at-risk event is escalated before the window closes, with Compliance notified of any that will be missed.

checklist.step: Assess and report any notice delivered outside its window
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any notice with a dispatch timestamp outside its statutory window.
Assess whether the delay caused customer detriment (e.g. a renewal lapsed before the customer was notified of a repriced premium).
Where detriment is found, initiate the customer remediation process (extension, reinstatement, goodwill payment as appropriate).
Record the root cause and remediation in the tracker.
checklist.done: every late notice has an assessed detriment finding and, where warranted, a tracked remediation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the notice log to the AI decision event log monthly
actions: Pull the AI-influenced decision events (declines, repricings, claims decisions) from the underwriting/claims workstation event log.
Compare to the notice log for the same period and identify any decision event with no matching notice record.
Route any gap to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for immediate investigation.
Record the reconciliation outcome monthly.
checklist.done: the notice log is reconciled to the decision event log monthly with any gap routed for investigation.

checklist.step: Review delivery-channel effectiveness quarterly
actions: Analyse the bounce/undeliverable rate by channel (post vs email vs portal) quarterly.
Identify any channel with a materially higher failure rate and investigate the cause (stale addresses, spam filtering).
Recommend channel-priority rule changes to the Policy Admin Ops Lead where warranted.
Record the quarterly review outcome.
checklist.done: channel effectiveness is reviewed quarterly with any material failure-rate issue investigated and addressed.

checklist.step: Audit a sample of notices for content accuracy
actions: Pull a monthly sample of 10 dispatched notices across the three notice types.
Confirm the merged content (decision reason, figures, dates) matches the underlying policy/claims record exactly.
Flag any content error and route to Policy Administration Analyst for correction and, if already sent, a corrected re-issue.
Record the audit outcome monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly content-accuracy sample is completed with any error corrected and re-issued where already dispatched.

checklist.step: Update the delivery-window rules on any regulatory change
actions: Monitor FCA Handbook updates to ICOBS and DISP delivery-timing requirements.
Update the Notice Generation and Delivery Procedure and the system's window configuration where a rule changes.
Notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead and re-test the trigger configuration for the changed window.
Record the update date and the re-test outcome.
checklist.done: delivery-window rules are updated and re-tested within 30 days of any relevant FCA rule change.

checklist.step: Confirm claims-decision notices align with the claims file
actions: For claims-decision notices, cross-check the notice's stated decision and reason against the claims file's recorded outcome and adjuster notes.
Flag any mismatch between the AI-influenced triage outcome and the notice text before dispatch where the workflow allows a pre-send check.
Escalate systemic mismatches to the Model Risk Analyst for the underlying model documentation to be reviewed.
Record the check outcome.
checklist.done: claims-decision notices are checked against the claims file, with mismatches flagged before or promptly after dispatch.

checklist.step: Retain the notice log and delivery evidence
actions: Export the notice log with delivery proofs into the compliance evidence repository quarterly.
Apply the 7-year-from-lapse/closure retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by policy number and notice type.
Verify prior quarters' exports remain retrievable.
checklist.done: the notice log and delivery evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by policy number.

testing.step: Build the population of decision events triggered in the quarter
actions: Extract every decline, renewal-repricing and claims-decision event from the policy administration system's event log for the quarter.
Reconcile the extract count to the notice log's trigger count for the same period.
List any event with no matching notice log entry as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the notice log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of events already flagged late or undeliverable in the notice log.
Take 25 randomly selected on-time events, minimum 10 per notice type (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every already-flagged late event.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory delivery window for each sampled event
actions: Independently recompute the required delivery window from the decision date using the current rule (5 business days decline, 21 calendar days renewal, 3 business days claims-decision).
Compare to the logged dispatch timestamp and flag any breach not already caught.
Cross-check business-day calculations against the bank holiday calendar in force at the time.
Record findings by policy number.
testing.done: delivery-window compliance is independently recomputed and any unflagged breach is logged as a new exception.

testing.step: Verify content accuracy against the source decision record
actions: Pull the actual dispatched notice text and compare every merged field (decision reason, premium figures, dates) to the underlying policy or claims record.
Flag any content mismatch as an exception.
Confirm the notice template version used matches the version approved and mapped for that decision type at the time.
Record findings by policy number.
testing.done: content accuracy and template version currency are independently verified for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Trace delivery proof for each sampled notice
actions: Confirm a delivery proof (send confirmation, mail house dispatch confirmation) exists and matches the logged channel.
For bounced/undeliverable cases, confirm a re-dispatch occurred within 2 business days per procedure, or an escalated manual attempt is documented.
Flag any notice with no delivery proof and no bounce-handling record.
Record findings by policy number.
testing.done: delivery proof or documented bounce-handling is confirmed for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Verify detriment assessment on every late notice
actions: For each sampled late notice, confirm a detriment assessment was performed and documented.
Where detriment was found, confirm the remediation (extension, reinstatement, goodwill payment) was actually completed.
Flag any late notice with no detriment assessment on file.
Record findings by policy number.
testing.done: detriment assessment and, where warranted, remediation completion is confirmed for every sampled late notice.

testing.step: Check the monthly reconciliation and content-accuracy audit records
actions: Confirm the monthly notice-log-to-decision-event reconciliation was performed for every month in the quarter.
Confirm the monthly content-accuracy sample audit was performed and any error corrected.
Flag any missed monthly control as a process exception.
Record findings.
testing.done: monthly reconciliation and content-accuracy audit performance is confirmed for the full quarter.

testing.step: Assess channel-failure trends
actions: Independently compute the bounce/undeliverable rate by channel for the quarter.
Compare to the Customer Experience Lead's quarterly review conclusions.
Flag any material discrepancy or unaddressed high-failure channel.
Record findings.
testing.done: channel-failure trends are independently recomputed and compared to the internal quarterly review.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the policy number, what was missed and the customer impact.
Assign a root cause (trigger failure, content error, delivery failure, missed reconciliation) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm any required customer remediation was completed.
Carry unresolved items into next quarter's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed statutory windows causing customer detriment.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed none of the sampled notices, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Translate the compliance requirement into a system change request
actions: Take the approved timing/content rule from Compliance (e.g. a new delivery-window figure, a revised notice content mapping) and open a change request in the ITSM platform.
Write the requirement as a testable acceptance criterion: trigger condition, exact timing threshold, expected system behaviour.
Link the change request to the source compliance procedure or policy version it implements.
Route to the Head of IT for prioritisation into the release backlog.
checklist.done: the change request states a testable acceptance criterion and is linked to its source compliance requirement.

checklist.step: Design the configuration in the business rules engine
actions: In the policy administration platform's business rules engine, build or amend the rule implementing the trigger condition and timing threshold.
Where content is affected, link the rule to the correct managed content block from the notice text library rather than hard-coding text.
Document the rule logic (inputs, condition, output) in the change record.
Peer-review the rule design with another Configuration Engineer before build.
checklist.done: the rule design is documented, peer-reviewed and correctly references the managed content block.

checklist.step: Write compliance test cases covering the acceptance criteria
actions: Write test cases covering the happy path (trigger fires within the window), boundary conditions (event on the exact deadline day) and failure modes (missing data preventing trigger).
Include a test case for weekend/bank-holiday handling on business-day-based windows.
Include a content test case confirming the merged notice text matches the current approved version exactly.
Link each test case to its source acceptance criterion in the change request.
checklist.done: test cases cover happy path, boundary conditions, failure modes and content accuracy, each linked to an acceptance criterion.

checklist.step: Execute the test cases in the UAT environment
actions: Deploy the configuration change to the UAT environment.
Execute every linked test case, recording pass/fail and evidence (screenshot, generated document, timestamp log) for each.
Log any failure as a defect against the Configuration Engineer with reproduction steps.
Re-test after any defect fix until 100% of test cases pass.
checklist.done: 100% of linked test cases pass in UAT with evidence captured for each.

checklist.step: Obtain Compliance sign-off on the UAT evidence
actions: Review the UAT test evidence against the original compliance requirement.
Confirm the boundary-condition and content-accuracy test cases specifically demonstrate the rule is enforced as intended.
Sign off in the change record, or return with specific gaps for rework.
Record the sign-off date.
checklist.done: Compliance has signed off the UAT evidence as demonstrating the requirement is correctly enforced.

checklist.step: Promote the change to production under segregation of duties
actions: Confirm the release pipeline shows a 100% pass on linked compliance test cases before allowing promotion.
Promote the change using a release engineer distinct from the Configuration Engineer who built it.
Record the deployment timestamp and the build/release identifiers in the change record.
Notify the Configuration Engineer and Compliance Officer of successful deployment.
checklist.done: the change is promoted by a segregated releaser only after the pipeline confirms 100% test pass, with deployment logged.

checklist.step: Run a production smoke test immediately after deployment
actions: Execute a subset of the compliance test cases against the live production environment using a non-customer-impacting test record where possible.
Confirm the trigger fires and the content renders exactly as it did in UAT.
Escalate any production-only discrepancy to the Configuration Engineer immediately and consider a rollback.
Record the smoke test result in the change record.
checklist.done: a production smoke test confirms the change behaves as tested, with any discrepancy triggering an immediate escalation.

checklist.step: Roll back immediately if production does not match tested behaviour
actions: On confirmation of a production discrepancy, authorise an immediate rollback to the last known-compliant configuration.
Notify Compliance and the business owner of the rollback and the customer-impact window, if any.
Open an incident record covering root cause investigation.
Do not re-attempt promotion until the root cause is fixed and re-tested end to end.
checklist.done: any production discrepancy triggers an immediate rollback, notification and incident record before re-attempting the change.

checklist.step: Monitor configuration drift after deployment
actions: Set up an automated monthly check comparing the live rules-engine configuration to the last approved, signed-off baseline.
Alert the Configuration Engineer and Compliance Officer on any unauthorised drift.
Investigate drift causes (emergency hotfix, manual override) and require retrospective compliance sign-off.
Record the monthly drift-check outcome.
checklist.done: a monthly automated drift check runs, with any unauthorised change investigated and retrospectively signed off.

checklist.step: Maintain the requirements-to-configuration traceability matrix
actions: Maintain a matrix linking every active compliance rule to its implementing configuration item and its most recent test evidence.
Update the matrix on every change deployment.
Review the matrix quarterly for any compliance rule with no linked, currently-tested configuration.
Route gaps to the Head of IT for prioritisation.
checklist.done: the traceability matrix is current and reviewed quarterly, with gaps routed for prioritisation.

checklist.step: Run a full annual regression test of all timing/content configurations
actions: Assemble the full library of compliance test cases across all notice types and timing rules.
Automate execution against a full-scale UAT refresh mirroring production configuration.
Record pass/fail for every rule and route failures to the Configuration Engineer for remediation before the next release window.
Report the annual regression result to the Head of IT and Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the full annual regression test is executed with results reported and failures remediated before the next release.

checklist.step: Review access controls on the rules engine
actions: Review who holds production write-access to the business rules engine and correspondence template designer quarterly.
Confirm access is limited to authorised Configuration Engineers and Release Coordinators, with no direct business-user write access.
Remove access for anyone who has left the role or no longer needs it.
Record the access review outcome quarterly.
checklist.done: production write-access to the rules engine is reviewed quarterly and restricted to authorised roles.

checklist.step: Log configuration exceptions and track to closure
actions: Raise a ticket for any configuration deployed without a passed compliance test case, any drift finding, or any smoke-test discrepancy.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Track the ticket to closure with re-test evidence attached.
Report open exceptions monthly to the Head of IT and Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: every configuration exception is ticketed, assigned, remediated and closed with re-test evidence.

checklist.step: Update the System Configuration Change Standard on process learnings
actions: Review incident and exception patterns from the past year for recurring root causes.
Propose Standard updates (additional mandatory test case types, tighter segregation rules) where warranted.
Route the proposed update through Head of IT and Head of Compliance for approval.
Publish and communicate the updated Standard to all Configuration Engineers.
checklist.done: the Standard is reviewed annually against incident patterns and updated where warranted.

checklist.step: Retain the configuration change and test evidence
actions: File each change request, rule design, test case results, sign-offs and deployment log into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-retirement retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by change request ID and the compliance rule it implements.
Verify prior changes remain retrievable alongside the current configuration.
checklist.done: the configuration change evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by change request ID.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration changes deployed in the quarter
actions: Extract every configuration change deployed to production in the quarter that touches notice timing or content rules from the ITSM platform.
Reconcile the extract to the release pipeline's deployment log.
List any deployment found in the pipeline log with no matching ITSM change request as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the deployment log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of changes flagged as rolled back or exception-logged during the quarter.
Take 10 randomly selected clean deployments (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every rolled-back or exception-logged change.

testing.step: Re-perform the compliance test cases against the live configuration
actions: Independently re-execute the boundary-condition and content-accuracy test cases against the current production configuration for each sampled change.
Compare results to the original UAT and smoke-test evidence.
Flag any test case that now fails, or that was never actually executed despite being marked passed.
Capture the re-performance evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled change's compliance test cases are independently re-executed with any failure or fabricated pass logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the traceability from compliance requirement to deployed rule
actions: For each sampled change, confirm the ITSM change request links to a specific, dated compliance requirement or policy version.
Confirm the deployed rule logic in the change record matches the stated acceptance criterion.
Flag any change with a vague or missing requirement linkage.
Record findings by change request ID.
testing.done: requirement-to-configuration traceability is independently confirmed for every sampled change.

testing.step: Confirm segregation of duties on promotion
actions: Confirm the individual who promoted each sampled change to production is different from the Configuration Engineer who built it.
Confirm the compliance sign-off predates the promotion timestamp.
Flag any change promoted by its own builder or without a pre-dated sign-off.
Record findings by change request ID.
testing.done: segregation of duties and sign-off sequencing is independently confirmed for every sampled change.

testing.step: Test the monthly configuration drift-detection control
actions: Confirm the drift-detection check ran every month in the quarter with results retained.
Independently compare the current production configuration to the last approved baseline for the sampled rules.
Flag any drift not caught by the monthly control.
Record findings.
testing.done: drift-detection control performance is confirmed for the quarter and any missed drift is independently identified.

testing.step: Verify rollback handling on any flagged discrepancy
actions: For each sampled change that triggered a rollback, confirm an incident record exists with a documented root cause.
Confirm the re-attempted deployment carried updated test cases addressing the root cause.
Confirm any affected customers or transactions during the discrepancy window were identified and assessed for impact.
Record findings by change request ID.
testing.done: rollback handling, root-cause fix and customer-impact assessment are confirmed for every sampled rollback.

testing.step: Review production access controls
actions: Independently pull the current access list for the business rules engine and correspondence template designer.
Compare against the last quarterly access review and confirm all listed individuals are current and authorised.
Flag any unauthorised or stale access not caught by the quarterly review.
Record findings.
testing.done: production access is independently reviewed and any gap missed by the quarterly control is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a ticket per exception with the change request ID, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (missing test case, sign-off gap, segregation failure, undetected drift) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next quarter's mandatory retest.
Confirm prior-quarter exceptions were genuinely closed before marking them resolved.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest status.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for changes deployed without a passed compliance test case.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who built none of the sampled changes, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
